correctness.rationale: For fixed interior alpha the tilt is a product measure, preserves the law on every root-count level and has a unique finite positive parameter. The interior Bernoulli variance is linear in n. Fourier inversion gives the local probability at floor(alpha n): near zero the centered log characteristic function is -Var(N)s^2/2+O(n|s|^3), and the sin^2 bound controls the remaining Fourier integral. The mean counts satisfy the stated triangular linear recurrence; normalized by n this is Euler's method with step 1/(n-1), order-one smooth coefficients, and a vanishing grid and normalization discrepancy. The time-changed Yule transition is geometric and t/q(t) has derivative p(t)/q(t), which proves conservation of size mass. Replacing a single independent choice cuts and reattaches at most one descendant subtree, affecting at most four old/new count contributions. Exponential concentration therefore transfers across the order n^(-1/2) conditioning event. Fixed-k convergence and equal unit size mass control both tails beyond a fixed K and yield weighted l1 and the two total-variation kernels. The supplied finite verifier was inspected, not used as proof of the exact-conditioning limit.

value.rationale: The typical density alone misses a natural family of atypical forest laws. The result gives the complete explicit component spectrum for every interior density and controls vertex mass, not merely typical-component probabilities. That control is needed for the uniform-vertex law and excludes escape of mass into sizes beyond any finite observation window as that window grows.
